status: frozen real-measurement case registry; column semantics and horizon class fixed before scoring
label_basis: horizon class declared from the measured phenomenon and its primary source, never from an EPOCH score

excluded_subset_files.CHWIRUT2: subset of CHWIRUT1; shares mechanism group ultrasonic_attenuation and adds no independent unit
excluded_subset_files.CLARK2: CLARK3 is its 1/5 decimation; shares mechanism group bose_gas_density and adds no independent unit

cases.column_note: the numeric block stores (temperature, coefficient); the header text lists the response first, so the order was fixed against the certified StRD values (first point: 24.41 K, 0.591)
cases.incumbent_1899: temperature-independent expansion coefficient from classical equipartition of lattice modes
cases.why: the measured coefficient falls towards zero below the Debye temperature, which equipartition cannot produce
cases.source: T. Hahn, copper thermal expansion study, NIST (1970s); NIST StRD HAHN1

cases.incumbent_1899: no persistent screening currents; classical Ohmic decay of an induced magnetization
cases.why: magnetization relaxation of a superconductor has no pre-1900 account
cases.source: L. Bennett, L. Swartzendruber and H. Brown, NIST (April 1994); NIST StRD BENNETT5

cases.incumbent_1899: Maxwell-Boltzmann density profile of a classical gas
cases.why: the density profile of a degenerate Bose gas requires quantum statistics
cases.source: C. Clark, Physics Laboratory, NIST (1995); NIST Dataplot CLARK3, a 1/5 decimation of CLARK2

cases.incumbent_1899: empirical Rydberg series with a fitted series constant (Rydberg 1888)
cases.why: the file is a bare (n, term energy) block for a sulfur Rydberg series; the measured curve follows an inverse-square series that was available empirically before 1900, so the declared horizon already predicts it
cases.column_note: the file carries no header; the certified StRD response (the quantum defect itself) is absent, and the second column is the StRD predictor
cases.source: R. Roszman, quantum defects for sulfur, NIST; NIST StRD ROSZMAN1 predictor block

cases.why: the two-carrier reduction of the measured curve rests on band theory
cases.source: Kim, electron mobility analysis, NIST (June 1992); NIST Dataplot KIM

cases.incumbent_1899: classical free-electron transport with density-independent mobility
cases.why: the measured mobility-density relation rests on band structure and impurity scattering
cases.source: R. Thurber, semiconductor electron mobility, NIST; NIST StRD THURBER

cases.incumbent_1899: attenuated elastic-wave propagation with geometric spreading
cases.why: classical acoustics covers the measured attenuation
cases.source: D. Chwirut, ultrasonic reference-block calibration, NIST; NIST StRD CHWIRUT1

cases.incumbent_1899: classical wave-optical interference in a circular aperture
cases.why: a sharp transmission resonance is morphologically unusual but fully classical; this is the shape-versus-physics hard control
cases.source: K. Eckerle, circular interference transmittance, NIST; NIST StRD ECKERLE4

cases.incumbent_1899: Hookean elastic response with a small quadratic correction
cases.why: classical elasticity covers the measured deflection
cases.source: P. Pontius, NIST load-cell calibration; NIST StRD PONTIUS

cases.why: an electron-microscope line-width standard is a metrology transfer curve, not a physical law
cases.source: R. Kirby, electron-microscope line-width standards, NIST; NIST StRD KIRBY2

cases.why: a radiographic calibration curve is a metrology transfer curve, not a physical law
cases.source: Berger, Alaska pipeline ultrasonic defect calibration, NIST; NIST StRD BERGER1

cases.why: an optical imaging calibration line is a metrology transfer curve, not a physical law
cases.source: C. Croarkin, optical imaging linewidth calibration, NIST; NIST Dataplot CALIBRATIONLINE

cases.incumbent_1899: classical dielectric relaxation of a polymer
cases.why: complex impedance dispersion is classical electromagnetism
cases.source: Bates and Watts (1988) p. 280 polymer impedance; NIST Dataplot WATTODR3

cases.incumbent_1899: slow monotone instrument drift about a stable reference value
cases.why: a five-year standard-resistor record is an instrument stability series
cases.source: R. Dziuba, standard resistors 1980-1985, NIST (July 1986); NIST Dataplot DZIUBA1
